jobs.occupation: Technical Service Engineer – European Region (full-time, m/f/d) (Außendienstmitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Absen Optoelectronic Co., Ltd., founded in 2001, is a global leader in LED display manufacturing, renowned for its innovation, reliability, and customer-centric approach. With over 3,000 employees worldwide, we provide cutting-edge LED display solutions across diverse industries.Absen GmbH, founded in 2013, is the German subsidiary of the Absen Group, headquartered in Mörfelden-Walldorf near Frankfurt am Main. It directly manages the European market, coordinating all sales, service, and logistics activities across Europe, working closely with customers and partners, and ensuring that Absen’s high-quality standards are consistently met.Technical Service Engineer – European Region (full-time, m/f/d)Location: Mörfelden-Walldorf, Germany (near Frankfurt am Main)Reporting to: European Service ManagerRole OverviewWe are looking for a Technical Service Engineer to join our local service team in Germany and work closely with the European service organization.Reporting to the European Service Manager, you will receive comprehensive onboarding training and ongoing business guidance to help you quickly gain an understanding of our products, customer service processes, and internal systems, enabling you to successfully integrate into the team and take ownership of your responsibilities.Responsibilities- Provide technical consultation, troubleshooting and solution support to customers and partners via phone, email, instant messaging and remote diagnostic tools.- Diagnose and resolve LED display hardware and software issues remotely and on-site. Prepare detailed fault analysis and service reports.- Act as the technical point of contact for end customers, system integrators and channel partners across Europe, handling technical inquiries, service requests and escalations.- Travel across Europe to customer sites as required to provide installation guidance, commissioning, maintenance and repair support, ensuring successful project acceptance and delivery.- Provide technical training to customers and partners on product operation, routine maintenance, system commissioning, troubleshooting and LED module repair.- Coordinate with internal teams to ensure timely resolution of customer issues and contribute to continuous improvements in service quality and customer satisfaction.Qualification- Technical education or vocational training in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, Telecommunications, or a related field; a bachelor’s degree or above is a plus.- Relevant professional experience in technical service, field service, or a related technical role. Experience in the LED display or AV industry is a strong advantage.- Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.- Fluent English required; German proficiency is a plus, with Chinese proficiency also considered an advantage.- Strong customer-oriented mindset with excellent interpersonal and communication skills.- Willingness to travel extensively across Europe, approximately 50%–70%, and ability to work independently on customer-facing on-site assignments.- Detail-oriented, well-organized, and capable of working with a structured and systematic approach.What We Offer- A supportive, collaborative, and international working environment.- A flat organizational structure with efficient and open communication.- A competitive compensation package.- Comprehensive onboarding and continuous professional development opportunities.- 30 days of paid annual leave per year.- Flexible working hours.- Travel allowances and comprehensive support for business trips.- Birthday and Christmas benefits.- Free coffee and beverages in the office.- Free parking.Become part of the Absen family!We look forward to welcoming you to the Absen family!Please send your complete application to: wlong@absen-europe.com (https://mailto:wlong@absen-europe.com) .

Are you interested in communication, social media and digital content? Are you an enthusiast of European cooperation like we are? Our projects work towards a more resilient, greener Baltic Sea region, making it a more attractive place to live. But Interreg is more than EU funding. It brings together people, perspectives and expertise from different countries to jointly develop solutions that travel across borders.Our Rostock-based team is international, and our working language is English. As part of the communication team, you will help us tell the stories behind our projects, create content for digital channels and make the results of European cooperation visible across the Baltic Sea region. You will find more information about us here: www.interreg-baltic.eu (http://www.interreg-baltic.eu) .What will you do:- Create communication content, including social media posts, articles, presentations, images and multimedia content;- Help manage and develop our social media presence;- Update content on our Programme portal using WordPress;- Help prepare newsletters and other digital communication;- Support the organisation of physical and online events and meetings;- Help keep communication materials and documentation well organised;- Occasionally substitute the Office Manager during absences.Expected qualifications and profile:- A degree, an ongoing education or relevant practical experience in communication, marketing, media or a related field;- Fluent in oral and written English; command of German is an advantage;- Confidence using MS Office, particularly PowerPoint, Word and Excel;- An interest and practical experience in digital communication, social media and creating visual or video content;- Experience with a content management system, ideally WordPress, is an advantage;- An interest in the Baltic Sea region, European cooperation and EU-related topics;- Attention to detail and a structured, reliable approach to work.Terms of employmentThe position will be a full-time contract (38 working hours a week) based on German employment law. Part-time work is an option as well. You will report to the Team Leader Programme Unit, and the MA/JS director. The employer will be Investitionsbank Schleswig-Holstein (IB.SH) as the hosting institution of the Managing Authority/Joint Secretariat. The place of employment will be in Rostock, Germany. A part of the weekly worktime you can work from another location. The contract duration will be until 31 December 2029. The annual gross salary will range between EUR 43,000 and 50,000, depending on qualifications and experience.Application and selection procedureApplications have to be submitted electronically in English by 11 November 2026 to the following email address: jobs@interreg-baltic.eu (https://mailto:jobs@interreg-baltic.eu) .Applications have to include the following documents:- Motivation video: Present yourself in a short video (up to 3 minutes, MP4 format). Tell us more about yourself: your experience in communication and your particular strengths. Tell us what interests you most in communication and why. Explain your motivation to join our team in Rostock.- CV based on Europass standard template (https://europa.eu/europass/en/create-europass-cv (https://europa.eu/europass/en/create-europass-cv) ) These documents will constitute the basis for selecting candidates for job interviews. Interviews are planned for December 2026. We might contact candidates during the selection process. The selected candidate is expected to start as soon as possible. ContactEeva Rantama, Team Leader Programme Unit, eeva.rantama@interreg-baltic.eu (https://mailto:eeva.rantama@interreg-baltic.eu) ; phone: +49 163 600 5254Anna Gałyga, Senior Communication Officer/Deputy Team Leader, anna.galyga@interreg-baltic.eu (https://mailto:anna.galyga@interreg-baltic.eu) ; phone: +49 163 600 5277Homeoffice:Umfang: Maximal 50%

Are you ready to start your career as an Aircraft Test Engineer (d/f/m)? This role works directly with state-of-the-art aviation systems. Located in Finkenwerder, you'll join a team tasked with providing Ground Test Instructions (GTIs) and Re-Test Instructions (RTIs) for the A320 family, across sites in Hamburg, Tianjin, and Alabama. Your efforts will directly support progress in the aerospace industry, helping ensure that modifications and functional tests are carried out to the highest standards. In a full-time position, you’ll take on a complex role that combines engineering creativity with operational excellence.- You will plan and develop functional tests, such as GTIs and RTIs, using construction documents and Ground Test Requirements (GTR).- You will take part in cross-border coordination and assess whether GTR content is feasible.- You will track modifications and verify their effect on both existing and newly created GTIs.- You will make sure GTR is fully applied in aircraft-specific GTIs.- You will give direct assistance during function test execution and resolve issues in aircraft and test systems.- You will play a key role in developing and enhancing testing tools and facilities.- You will plan, carry out, and oversee projects aimed at lowering function test costs.- You will help improve the test system specifications after any aircraft modifications.- Drawing on your expertise, you will contribute to solving critical issues, including resolutions related to Ground Test Instructions up to Rejected Take-Off (RTO).VORAUSSSETZUNGEN:If you are eager to take on a demanding and technical position in the aviation sector, this role could be ideal for you. To be successful, you will need a solid background in engineering, technical documentation, and troubleshooting within complex aerospace or electronic systems. The qualifications and skills needed for this position are listed below:- Minimum Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a comparable technical discipline.- Minimum 2-3 years of professional experience in aviation, electronics, engineering, or technical documentation.- Proficiency with tools such as SAP, Taksy/Gesy/Tesy, and zamiz, as well as familiarity with Google Workspace environments.- Strong technical knowledge of communication and information systems, with more than three years of experience.- Fluent in English (advanced working proficiency) and German (proficiency).- Proven ability to understand and assess complex technical designs and workflows.- A proactive, organized, and results-driven approach to project management and teamwork.- Excellent communication skills to work effectively across all levels of an organization.- Willingness to travel internationally 1-2 times per year and occasionally be available on-call.Benefits:This full-time role comes with a competitive, well-rounded benefits package aimed at helping you thrive professionally while keeping a healthy balance between work and personal life. Main benefits include:- An open-ended employment contract for greater job security.- A 35-hour working week to support work-life balance.- 30 days of paid annual leave to rest and recover.- An annual salary based on an appealing Equal Pay model.- Flexibility for additional hours, either as compensatory time off or financial compensation.

As the Version Planer (d/m/w), you will hold a key position within the A320 Program Management department in Finkenwerder. You will support smooth collaboration and coordination among multiple operational teams, including configuration management, production, engineering, procurement, and transport. Your work will directly support the delivery of important company goals, with a strong focus on meeting customer commitments on time.- Develop, roll out, track, and oversee the Integrated Programme Planning to ensure it remains robust and relevant.- Foresee and handle planning deviations to keep project timelines on track and improve financial outcomes.- Work with cross-functional contracts and teams to align commercial needs with operational possibilities.- Set up and maintain end-to-end Integrated Version Planning for key versions of interest (HoV and VoI).- Represent Integrated Planning in Fulfill Customer Order (FCO) Core Teams and Multifunctional Teams.- Support lead-time recovery and reduction initiatives to improve productivity.- Comply with departmental frameworks for structured, outcome-driven project delivery.VORAUSSSETZUNGEN:We are looking for a candidate who has a demonstrated track record of handling complex integrated planning processes in an international and varied environment. jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)(full time / part time options available)Location: GörlitzEmployment scope: full time / part time options are availableType of contract: initially limited to three years; the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluationRemuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum program. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleaguesYour tasks- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.- Secure external research funds.- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programs of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.Your profile - Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team- Very good command of German (B2)- Fluency in English, both spoken and written- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstancesDesirable skills - Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology- Knowledge in research data management and databases- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum workWe offer - Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology- A working place in completely new building with dissection and other laboratories, collection rooms, in the historic town of Görlitz with rapidly developing local research community (DZA, CASUS, IHI/TUD, HiLusatia), yet situated very close to nature with high mammal diversity and opportunities for field work- Opportunities to participate in teaching and outreach activities, e.g., in our museum and with collaborating universities- Opportunities for establishing an independent academic working group and acquiring further academic qualifications- Flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card  with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement  – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability, they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply? Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) as a single PDF file by November 10, 2026https://www.senckenberg.de/de/stellenanzeigen/.For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/ (https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/)For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de (http://www.senckenberg.de)Contact Senckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.Homeoffice:Umfang: Maximal 40%

jobs.occupation: 23 Interdisciplinary PhD positions in Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials – IMPRS UFAST (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: The International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging and Structural Dynamics in Hamburg, Germany, offers a structured PhD program focusing on ultra-fast phenomena, X-ray physics and dynamical imaging in all areas of science covering physics, chemistry and biology.23 Interdisciplinary PhD positions in Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials – IMPRS UFAST – HamburgResearchThe program offers exciting research opportunities at ultra-intense electron and X-ray sources to directly observe atomic motions during primary events. The use of ultrafast imaging over the relevant length and time scales generates new levels of understanding of the interplay between structure and dynamics. Specific areas include the theoretical and experimental aspects of quantum materials and atomically resolved dynamics, fundamental light-matter interaction, accelerator-based light sources, coherent controlled molecular and solid state dynamics, molecular imaging, extreme timescale spectroscopy, ultrafast optics and X-ray scienceWe offer:- A range of PhD positions in these areas: open positions (https://www.mpsd.mpg.de/350422/open_phd_projects)- State-of-the-art research facilities on an extensive science campus- Cross-disciplinary research in a vibrant, international scientific environment- First class supervision and mentorship by a team of internationally renowned experts- Outstanding training in your scientific subject and transferable skills (in English)- A 3-year employment contract based on the German federal pay agreementRequirementsWe seek applicants with an excellent academic background. You hold (or are about to complete) an MSc degree or equivalent in physics, chemistry or related areas. You need to be passionate about research in ultrafast phenomena and motivated to conduct rigorous scientific work over the full degree period.ApplyApplications must be submitted via the [online application portal](https://jobs.b-ite.com/en/jobposting/760bb8588f9051b5f5b84840eb91eff55142a8780/apply)The application deadline is 06th November 2026. PhD projects start in summer/autumn 2026. In exceptional cases, it may possible to start on the research project earlier. For any further questions or problems regarding the application process or the online system, please contact the IMPRS UFAST coordinator on IMPRS.UFAST@mpsd.mpg.de.

Experience with stage-gate or similar product development methodologies.•Communication Skills: Good written and verbal communication skills (German and English). The ability to articulate complex technical and business concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. Desired Skills and Competencies•Innovation Focus: Skills to think out-of-the-box in an area which many experts consider that “everything has been invented”. Comfortable to challenge the status-quo and identify technologies (together with the R&D department) which could be a game change, innovate around use-cases, form/feature/function to improve the customer experience and business models.•Strategic Thinking: Ability to think strategically and develop a long-term vision for the product portfolio.•Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to analyze market data, customer feedback, and financial metrics to make data-driven decisions.•Customer-Centric: First experience how to gain and translate customer needs into product ideas and a passion for creating products that solve real-world problems.•Adaptability: Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic VUCA environment and adapt to changing market conditions and business priorities.•Team Player: A collaborative and team-oriented mindset. Ability to build strong relationships and work effectively with a diverse range of stakeholders.•Results-Oriented: A strong drive to achieve results and a commitment to excellence.Job RequirementsThe role will be based in the greater Düsseldorf/Cologne or the Hamburg metropolitan area and requires regular on-site time combined with appropriate home office opportunities. It also requires frequent national and international travel.Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.occupation: 586958 Systems Engineer & Technologist (all genders) (Forschungs- und Entwicklungsingenieur/in)
jobs.description: In this role, you will provide technical leadership for the development and lifecycle management of X-ray tubes, generators, and their subcomponents. By translating customer and business needs into robust system solutions and collaborating across multidisciplinary teams, you will help deliver innovative, reliable imaging technologies that drive Philips' success and create value for customers.Your role: - Define, introduce, and maintain system architectures for x-ray tubes, generators, and X-segments, including interfaces, system requirements, and modular building blocks. - Translate stakeholder, user, and business needs into clear, measurable, and traceable product requirements and design decisions. - Drive technology choices, design trade-off analyses, and the selection of suitable methods and tools to deliver balanced, robust solutions. - Lead system integration and verification, including the management of requirements, interfaces, and deviations through to system readiness. - Own technical and product risk assessments, define mitigations, and implement relevant medical standards and regulatory requirements – working across functions and with suppliers to continuously improve quality, reliability, and manufacturability. You should bring the following: - Master's degree or PhD in Engineering, Physics, Electrical, Mechanical, or a related technical field, with 5–10 years of relevant R&D experience.- Strong expertise in high-voltage X-ray generator design, power electronics, embedded systems, digital control, or X-ray tube technology.- Solid knowledge of physics, mechanical and electrical design, with strong analytical and systems architecture skills.- Experience with requirements management tools and systems engineering methodologies.- Proven technical leadership experience, with excellent stakeholder management, networking, and cross-functional collaboration skills.- Business-fluent in English and German, with the ability to manage complexity, influence stakeholders, and drive results.Doing meaningful work should come with fair, transparent rewards. The base salary range for this role is €118,606–€121,210.
